title: Resistance as a genetic object
dek: Most clinical Mtb resistance is chromosomal, target- or activation-site, sometimes efflux. Heteroresistance and disputed alleles are the genomics, not the footnote.
story: M. tuberculosis has no relevant horizontal plasmid DST story in the clinic. Resistance is almost always a chromosomal mutation: target modification (rpoB, gyrA, rrl, rrs), loss of a prodrug activator (katG, pncA, ddn/fbi), promoter overexpression of a target (inhA), or loss of a repressor that unleashes efflux (Rv0678).

MDR-TB is still defined around isoniazid plus rifampin. Pre-XDR adds fluoroquinolone resistance. XDR adds resistance to a Group A drug (bedaquiline or linezolid) on top of that. Definitions moved; genomes did not get the memo, so a 2015 “XDR” paper and a 2024 “XDR” paper are not the same object.

A mutation is a hypothesis about MIC, not a MIC. WHO catalogues grade genotype–phenotype association. Heteroresistance (mixed alleles in one culture or one lesion) can make a cartridge, a MGIT, and a WGS pileup tell three different short stories about the same patient.
deepTitle: Priors a computational lab should actually use
deep: Mutation supply scales with burden. Cavities are evolution experiments. Detecting a 5% rpoB S450L subpopulation is a different clinical object from a fixed allele, and variant callers with default 10% filters will lie to you.

Fitness is not optional flavor. S450L is common partly because it is tolerated, sometimes with rpoC compensatory mutations. Some pncA loss-of-function alleles are cheap; some gyrA D94G backgrounds pay more. Compensatory evolution is why you read the rest of RNAP, not only RRDR.

Critical concentrations are cut-points on an MIC distribution. Borderline rpoB alleles and moxifloxacin “breakpoint philosophy” are where a binary S/R column in a spreadsheet becomes propaganda. Report the allele, the grade, and the MIC if you have it.
Epistasis and lineage priors exist (eis promoter in L2, some phylogenetic markers mistaken for resistance). Always subtract the phylogenetic SNPs your catalogue already marked as not-associated.

example.title: A 8% S450L minority
example.setup: Direct sputum targeted NGS: rpoB S450L at 8% frequency. Xpert: RIF resistance not detected. MGIT culture later grows a RIF-susceptible majority with a resistant subcolony on 7H11.

steps.title: Three assays, three windows
steps.body: Xpert needs enough mutant template to drop a probe. 8% often will not. Targeted NGS with a 5% threshold sees it. MGIT critical-concentration DST can report S if the minority is outgrown.

steps.title: Do not average them
steps.body: This is heteroresistance, consistent with a mixed lesion or emerging resistance. Clinically it is a rifampin problem, not a voting exercise among assays.

steps.title: Caller settings are part of DST
steps.body: If your WGS pipeline filters variants below 10%, you will systematically miss this class. State the allele fraction in the report.

example.takeaway: Frequency is a clinical variable. Binary S/R columns throw it away.

check.prompt: MDR-TB is defined as resistance to:
check.why: That is still the MDR core. FQ makes pre-XDR; BDQ or LZD on top of MDR+FQ is the current XDR idea.

whyWrong.Bedaquiline plus linezolid: Group A drugs; that is not the MDR definition.

check.prompt: A pipeline reports no rpoB mutations because it drops variants with allele fraction < 0.10. A minority S450L at 8% will be:
choices: Silent in that pipeline, even though it can be clinically real
Proof that Xpert must be RIF-R
check.answer: Silent in that pipeline, even though it can be clinically real

whyWrong.Proof that Xpert must be RIF-R: Xpert often misses low-frequency minorities too.

check.prompt: In the mutation grid, which row is the teaching example of an Xpert-blind rifampin allele?
check.why: I491F sits outside the RRDR window. S450L is the opposite: the common Xpert-visible allele.

whyWrong.rpoB S450L: Inside RRDR; Xpert usually sees it.
